reviewed_stories.title: Number of ships transiting Strait of Hormuz falls to three on Wednesday, data shows
reviewed_stories.linkage: sector link for Oil & Gas Exploration; negative broad-market import and inflation risk
reviewed_stories.reason: Visible commodity vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz fell to three on Wednesday from 12 a day earlier, versus a 10-day average of about 17. The sharp deterioration is fresh physical evidence that the regional supply chokepoint remains materially impaired, which restores some upstream risk premium even though alternative Saudi routes are partly mitigating lost exports.

reviewed_stories.title: Oil prices extend losses as fears of Middle East supply disruptions ease
reviewed_stories.linkage: sector link for Oil & Gas Exploration relative to the supply-shock premium; positive broad-market import and inflation context
reviewed_stories.reason: Brent eased to about $105.64 as Saudi Arabia offered additional crude cargoes through Oman. The workaround reduces the probability of a larger sustained export loss, but analysts said it only partly offsets disrupted barrels and the pipeline outage remains unresolved, so the supply shock has softened rather than disappeared.

OGDC.reason: Brent remains above $100 and visible Hormuz commodity transits fell to just three from 12 a day earlier, versus a 10-day average near 17. Saudi cargoes through Oman partly mitigate disrupted exports, so the fresh physical chokepoint evidence restores some supply-risk premium without reversing the easing seen in spot crude.

MARI.reason: The collapse in visible Hormuz vessel traffic keeps regional upstream supply risk elevated while Brent remains above $100, although Saudi alternative cargoes reduce the expected severity of the disruption. Mari's gas-heavy production mix makes its direct crude sensitivity weaker than OGDC or PPL.
